text:
Jamie Oleksiak, the 6-foot-7 "Big Rig," came to Vancouver after 389 games in Seattle and has given the Canucks more offense than anyone should expect. He has 7 points in 18 games, against 15 all of last season, at 1.33 points per 60 minutes. Our range for him runs from 0.66 to 1.13, so some of this will cool: he has scored on 16.7% of his shots, more than double his usual rate.

The odd part is that his team has been unlucky with him on the ice, scoring 6.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve. His points are running hot while the five-on-five finishing around him runs cold. His relative 5v5 numbers are positive (+5.9), even inside a Canucks team that has won once in his last ten games.

His real job is defending. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%), with the weak spot in exits: only 26% kept possession. Watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes.
headline: Oleksiak's points are outrunning his shots
